firstScreen.notes: 1440-first.jpg: h1 'Albany carpentry, measured before it's priced' 6 words, 3 lines; phone in header and hero; Sample-rated proof line; ruler and elevation callouts visible. 390-first.jpg: h1 3 lines, both actions above the fold. Next band peeks only about 7px at 1440 (-0.5); primary action flips between hero (Call solid) and mobile bar (Price it orange) (-0.5).

distinctiveness.notes: 1440-full.jpg: section tags climb the pole in real heights (9 baseboard to 132 crown) and the footer ruler ends on 132 crown; every image is drawn in one drafting language; passes the cover-the-logo test. Mono micro-labels and middle-dot meta strings in most views (1440-first.jpg, 1440-scroll-50.jpg) (-0.5).

type.notes: 1440-scroll-75.jpg: Anybody pull-quote gives scale contrast; curly quotes, en-dash ranges, tabular numbers in hours and Sheet B-1 (1440-full.jpg). 3+ tiny tracked-caps labels in one view in 1440-scroll-50.jpg; ruler labels about 10px in 1440-first.jpg (-0.5).

layout.notes: 1440-full.jpg: 10 sections, alternating tones, no dark bands touching, full-bleed rowhouse drawing break, at least 6 layout families. #schedule does two jobs (hours plus guarantee) under a borrowed review heading (-0.5); #area is a thin beat.

photo.notes: 1440-full.jpg: no stock; every plate (door elevation, service details, probe section, Center Square rowhouse band, profiles, bookcase sheet) drawn in one line weight and ink, reading as one hand. No plan-to-result sequence; nothing shows a finished room.

copy.notes: 1440-scroll-50.jpg / 1440-full.jpg: trade nouns (dutchman, plinth, backband, profile gauge, knife ground, newel), honest 'The depth decides it.', doubt microcopy next to the form, Sample labels on every price, review, guarantee and the licence, no em dashes. #schedule heading lifts a customer review line as a slogan and does not describe the hours (1440-full.jpg).

mobile.notes: 390-first.jpg: story pole re-cut as a horizontal ruler, h1 3 lines, mobile bar with Call and Price it; render.json overflow clean at 320 and 390. 390-full.jpg: molding picker titles wrap 2-3 lines in 2 columns; hero elevation is the desktop drawing scaled down, not re-cut (-0.5).

a11y.notes: 1440-rm-full.jpg and 390-rm-full.jpg show all content and drawings; labelled inputs on planner, perimeter and ZIP (1440-full.jpg); round-2 empty footer anchors gone. Muted service-row text on the mid tone looks close to 4.5:1 (1440-scroll-25.jpg), verify it.

motion.notes: 1440-scroll-25/50/75.jpg: the active tick climbs the pole to each section height, a motion idea a visitor can name; the planner redraws live. The active label lags (9 baseboard label beside the 30 tick in 1440-scroll-25.jpg) and overprints the static 108 label in 1440-scroll-75.jpg (-0.5).

wow.notes: 1440-scroll-75.jpg / 1440-full.jpg #tool-builtin: planner output is a drawn 'SHEET B-1' elevation with bays, dimensions and a spec table, in the signature language, connected to the climbing pole. The molding picker output is still a text line plus bars (1440-scroll-50.jpg) (-0.5).

polish.notes: 1440-full.jpg footer: 'Price it' and the phone link sit off the nav baseline (also 390-full.jpg) (-0.5). 1440-full.jpg #brick left edge: clipped orange glyph; 1440-scroll-75.jpg: pole label overprints the 108 tick label (-0.5).

elevate.move: Make the footer ruler and the left story pole one finished drawing: same tick spacing, same labels at the same heights, one stroke weight and one label style for every tag and rule, so the page ends on the top of the pole the visitor climbed and looks like it came off one drafting table.

Put the hero elevation on the margin ruler's own 0-132 inch scale and draw it in on load, so each callout lines up with its tick and the ruler and doorway read as one measured object, and leave room under it for the services band to show.
